title: Component Patterns Applied Check
description: Practice choosing composition APIs, avoiding HOC and render-prop pitfalls, and designing controlled component patterns.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A Card needs customizable header, body, and footer areas. Which API is often a good fit?

options.text: Composition with children or named slot props

questions.explanation: Slots and children let callers place UI in well-defined areas without subclassing.

questions.prompt: An HOC injects a prop named user. What should you consider? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Avoid colliding with a user prop already supplied by callers
Pass unrelated props through to the wrapped component
Set a helpful displayName for debugging

questions.explanation: Good HOCs avoid prop collisions, preserve pass-through props, and keep debugging names clear.

questions.prompt: A render prop creates a new inline function each render and a memoized child still re-renders. Why?

options.text: The function prop has a new identity each render

questions.explanation: Function identity can defeat shallow memoization unless stabilized or designed around.

questions.prompt: Tabs.Tab and Tabs.Panel coordinate with Tabs state through context. What pattern is this?
questions.explanation: Compound components expose related pieces that share parent-managed state.

questions.prompt: Compound components still need accessibility concerns such as roles, labels, and keyboard behavior.
questions.explanation: Flexible composition does not remove accessibility responsibilities.

questions.prompt: A component can manage its own open state or accept open and onOpenChange from a parent. What is this supporting?
questions.explanation: Components can offer internal state by default while allowing callers to control state when needed.

questions.prompt: Which are good reasons to extract a custom hook instead of a container component? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: You want reusable stateful logic without prescribing markup
Multiple components need the same behavior with different UI
The logic is independent of a specific layout

questions.explanation: Custom hooks reuse behavior while letting each component choose its own presentation.

questions.prompt: A pattern makes a simple component harder to understand without reducing duplication. What should you do?

options.text: Convert it to an HOC automatically

questions.explanation: Patterns should solve real complexity; unnecessary abstraction hurts maintainability.
